findings.body: `shorten` trims whitespace then checks `text.chars().count() <= limit`. If the original text had leading/trailing whitespace, trimming can reduce the character count, but `limit` was presumably intended for the untrimmed text. More importantly, if trimmed length is exactly `limit`, the function returns the text unchanged only to have later add an `…` on the next path — but the early return prevents that. This is actually fine as written: the early return covers the equal case, and the later branch only runs when over limit. However, there is a subtlety: if the original string had trailing spaces, `text.trim()` removes them, and `text.chars().count()` may now be *less* than the caller expected. The function still returns the trimmed string, which is likely acceptable. No code change suggested because the logic is correct for its use case; the comment could clarify trimming rationale.
findings.title: Append ellipsis only when text exceeds limit after trimming

findings.body: `first_sentence` splits on the first `. ` (period, space) it finds. This will incorrectly truncate on strings like "Dr. Smith said..." or "Version 2.0 has..." or sentences containing decimal numbers. For the documented use case (a one-line summary of model-authored text), this is unlikely to cause real problems because check-run titles rarely contain such patterns, but it is a known heuristic limitation. Document this in the doc comment or use a more robust sentence boundary detection (e.g., from the `unicode-segmentation` crate).
findings.title: First-sentence extraction may split on abbreviations or numbers

value.summary: This pull request adds MongoDB deployment infrastructure for local development with a kernel bypass, enables embedding configuration, fixes environment variable names for GitHub App authentication, adds the `findings::summarise` module, and adjusts Docker Compose to mount the config file. The summarise logic has a corner case bug where `shorten` can append `…` even when already at or below the limit due to trimming, and `first_sentence` may incorrectly split on a period followed by a space that is part of an abbreviation or punctuation. However, the change is not intended to merge (it is an end-to-end test PR), so the findings are informational.
